0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 September 1986, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Measuring Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 Mains operated insulation resistance testers are convenient means of measuring insulation resistance on production line. They have the advantage over hand operated insulation resistance testers covered by IS : 2992-1980" or transistorized battery operated insulation resistance tester as the hand generator needs table space and both the hands of the operator get busy in operating the instrument, and batteries are difficult to maintain in daily use. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-19607. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value iu this standard.

1. 4.1 General - The tester shall be sufficiently robust to withstand mechanical vibrations and shocks. Its working parts shall be housed in a case which shall be dust proof and of sufficient strength to afford adequate protection against external damage. Housing shall be electricaly insulated. 4.2 Terminals - The tester shall be equipped with gaurd ring around the line terminal. A guard terminal shall also be provided and electrically connected to the gaurd ring in case of testers having rated resistance of 1 000 megohms and more; the line terminal, guard ring and 5

tS,119bk-1986 guard terminal shall be connected to the negative side and earth terminal to the positive side of the supply. The line terminal, guard terminal and earth terminal shall be suitably marked, preferably as L, G and E respectively to distinguish them. 4.3 Infinity Adjustment - Testers having rated resistance 1 000 M R and more shall be provided with a suitable device accessible from outside for adjusting the pointer to the infinity mark. 4.4 Pointer - The pointer shall enough to reach at least one-third 4.5 Central approximately have a knife-edge tip of small scale marks. mark range. and be be long

6.1 The rated input Loltage shall be the mains voltage ( single phase ), that is 230 V. However, the instrument should function within the specified limit for variation of the voltage. 6.2 Rated Output Voltage - The open circuit dc voltage at the testers between `line' and `earlh' terminals as assigned by the manufacturer. 7. GENERAL 7.1 Operation REQUIREMENTS of the Tester

7.1.1 The degree of damping of the moving system of the tester, that is the time elapsed till the pointer has been brought to a standstill, when a resistance of [he value corresponding to the central scale mark is inserted between the measuring terminals under normal conditions of use, shall not exceed three seconds. 8. 11.4 Insulation Resistance Test - The insulation resistance of the tester across all the external terminals connected together and the containing case and across all the external terminals connected together and the mains input when measured by applying 500 V dc, shall be not less than the values given below: a) For rated voltage up to and including above 250 V long enough 250 V 25 Mn 50 Mn to get a b) For rated voltage

IS : 11994 - 1986 11.5 High Voltage Test

11.5.1 No breakdown, arcing or sparking shall occur when an ac voltage of 2 000 volts ( rms ) is applied between all the live terminals connected together and the case for a period of one minute. 11.5.2 The value of 2 000 volts shall be applicable provided: 5 mA

1) The maximum steady state output current does not exceed ac and 10 mA dc or the mixed current 10 mA peak. 2) The rated output voltage is up to and including at In all other cases, the test shall be conducted twice the rated output voltage plus 1 000 volts. 11.6 Tests for Limits of Error to the provision voltage

11.6.1 Error Due to Variation of Level - A change of 5 degrees in the level of the tester, in any direction, shall not result in a deviation exceeding 0.5 mm of the pointer from its initial position. 11.6.2 Error Due to Variation of Ambient Temprature - The deviation of indicator of the tester shall not exceed 5 percent near the central scale mark for the ambient temperature change by 31 20�C from 27�C. 11.6.3 Error Due to Excessive Humidity - The error of the tester shall not exceed the limits specified in IS : 2992-1980* before and after recovery after an exposure of 24 hours to a relative humidty of 90 percent and at a temperature of 27�C. 11.6.4 Error Due to Stray Field - The error of the tester at the central mark shall not exceed f 5 percent of the indicated value, when the tester is exposed to a magnetic field produced by 400 ampere-turns ( dc ) in a The tester shall be so placed as to make the coil of one metre diameter. influence of the field maximum. 11.6.5 Ri/@e at measuring terminal Measuring Terminal - The shall not exceed 10 percent. lipple factor at the

IS : 11994 - 1986 11.8 Dust Test

11.8.1 The chamber of this test shall be capable of maintaining in any region inside it, where the tester may be placed, a temperature of 40 f 2�C and a relative humidity of not more than 80 percent. 11.8.2 The atmosphere within the chamber shall be agitated so as to keep it loaded with dust particles of such a size as to enable them to pass sieve with an aperture of 0'15 mm. through a wire mesh 150-micron The conThe bulk of the material of dust shall consist of free silica. centration of dust shall be determined by means of the device described in Appendix B where the requirement of dust concentration is also specified. 1X.8.3 The tester shall be placed in the test chamber for four hours with the atmosphere stirred and the dust shall then be allowed to settle for two hours. The tester shall then be removed from the chamber and shall satisfy the requirements given in 9. 11.9 Vibration Test in accordance with shall be as given

APPENDIX ( C~.LS~11.82 )
DUST B-l. DUST

B

CHAMBER AND APPARATUS FOR MEASURING DUST CONCENTRATION CHAMBER

B-l.1 A schematic layout of a typical chamber recommended for use for the dust cycle is shown in Fig. 1. It is designed to ensure uniform and The system is completely enclosed reproducible distribution of dust. A circulating fan, F and does not become congested during operation. ( low pressure, high volume ventilating pattern ) blows air over the pile, P where the dust is picked up and carried along into the chamber, C. The air velocity decreases in the chamber SO that much of the dust falls back into the hopper, H from where it returns to the pile, while the air is fed back into the fan through the top of the chamber. The dimensions of the hopper tube are so proportioned that whatever the head of the dust
*Methods for random sampling. 12

pressure may be, the pile P never completely fills the main air duct. Consequently, the air flow carries away, more or less, a constant amount of dust from a pile which all the time is being replenished.

B-2. APPARATUS

B-2.1 A simple measuring device is shown in Fig. 2. Dust enters the box through five circular holes and collects at the bottom of the detachable cover. For measuring dust concentration, the device is placed in any representative position within the dust chamber. The air is circulated for five minutes and the dust is then.allowed to settle down. The amount of dust which collects on the detachable cover during the total test period is weighed and shall be 23 f 5 g.
